result.title: Pulse: Long-Horizon Tasks Need Streaming Personalization
result.summary: Large language model agents increasingly undertake complex, long-horizon tasks that benefit from sustained personalized support through long-term memory. Existing memory-augmented methods retrieve and use memory primarily from the initial request, with limited awareness of ongoing execution and emerging personalization needs. Agents may therefore overlook user preferences and project constraints during multistep tasks. We propose Pulse, a streaming personalization method for long-horizon tasks. An independent, lightweight memory agent continuously monitors execution, identifies emerging personalization needs and potential preference conflicts, and uses user and project memories to provide targeted interventions at appropriate stages. Reinforcement learning optimizes when and how the memory agent intervenes, improving the timeliness and accuracy of personalized support. Pulse scores 71.9% on $π$-Bench and 46.4% on MCP-Persona, achieving the highest overall scores among the compared methods on both datasets while improving task execution efficiency.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Pulse，一种面向长时程任务的流式个性化方法：由一个独立的轻量 memory agent 持续监控执行过程，识别新出现的个性化需求与偏好冲突，并在合适阶段借助用户与项目记忆进行干预，同时用强化学习优化介入的时机与方式。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文与视觉/多模态推理无直接关系，但其「用 RL 学习何时、如何介入」的时序决策，可能与 LVR 中动态获取视觉证据、注入与停止的决策问题类比，可供核查；目前仅为概念层面的远距离线索。
